newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos says Singson need not resign.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos says Singson need not resign.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday rejected a call by leftist groups for central bank governor Gabriel Singson to resign after the peso plunged to a record low of 30 pesos this week.

"In the first place, he has not resigned. And in the second place, I don't think he should resign," Ramos said in a televised press conference when asked whether Singson has filed his resignation letter.
Leftist groups said Singson had reneged on his mandate to protect the integrity of the local currency when he allowed the peso to trade within a wider range on Friday.
The central bank had loosened its grip on the peso on hopes it would end months of speculation caused by Thailand's financial woes.
The central bank has said the peso is now showing signs of normalisation, trading at a higher range of 29/29.50 to the dollar on Wednesday.
